hints: Many patterns share prefixes, so searching for each separately wastes work.
Build a trie of all patterns and add failure links as in KMP.
Scan the text once with Aho-Corasick, then propagate visited states along failure links.
analogy: The trie is a shared dictionary; failure links tell you the longest useful suffix after a mismatch.
example: In text ababa, patterns aba and bab occur, while ac does not.
algorithm: Insert every pattern into a trie and build Aho-Corasick failure links in breadth-first order. Scan the text, recording which automaton states are visited. Propagate visits from each state to its failure parent in reverse breadth-first order. A pattern occurs exactly when its terminal state receives a visit.
correctness: At each text position the automaton state represents the longest dictionary prefix that is a suffix of the scanned text. Its failure ancestors represent all shorter such suffixes, so propagation marks exactly the patterns ending at some position.
complexity: For text length n, total pattern length L and fixed alphabet size 26, O(n+26L) time and O(26L) space.
